subject: Operator stewardship and license scope for on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cytechealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@cytechealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operator stewardship + license scope for our on-prem deployment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we liked the latency profile and the proposed VPC packaging. Legal at CyteHealth has asked us to collect a few specific items before we can proceed with an Order Form:

1) Clear license scope language for the private deployment: we need confirmation that the license is runtime-only (no distribution) and any restrictions on number of operator seats.
2) Operator stewardship/escrow-like options: in the event of a vendor outage or termination, we need a mechanism to get a verified snapshot of the deployed model assets + a forensic access path (read-only) to allow continuity for clinical inference.
3) Audit evidence: SOC2 logs, runbook excerpts, and a sample snapshot transfer checklist (we don't need the full snapshot now, just the process).
4) KMS / key handoff: can we put customer-managed KMS as an option, and how would temporary operator keys be handled?

I'm attaching a short list of the items Legal requested. Can you loop in your legal/ops folks and share a proposed addendum (MSA annex or Order Form exhibit) and an estimated timeline to produce the redline?

We are targeting a procurement review the week of Oct 18th.

Thanks,
Raj

--
Raj Patel
Director, Cloud Engineering
CyteHealth
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cytechealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator stewardship + license scope for our on-prem deployment

Hi Raj — thanks, and great question. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Lauren (deployments) so we can give you a single package.

Quick plan:
- Rishi: will draft a compact "Operator Stewardship" exhibit for the MSA that covers runtime-only license language, operator access limited to named accounts, and a snapshot-transfer protocol.
- Lauren: will provide a short runbook excerpt and the sample checklist you asked for.

Two clarifying asks for your legal team so our redline is precise:
A) When you say "forensic access path (read-only)", do you expect a full model artifact copy (weights + tokenizer + config) to be delivered, or a signed VM image/OCI snapshot that is verified by third-party steward?
B) Can we get a short list of required audit artifacts (e.g., retention window for logs, specific SOC2 controls you need evidence for)?

We can produce a redline + evidence bundle by COB Oct 9 if we get the clarifications above today. Does that timeline work for your procurement review?

Attachment: CyteHealth_Operator_Questions_20261007.pdf

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cytechealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Draft redline: Operator Stewardship exhibit + license carveouts

Folks — attaching a first-pass redline (file: Redline_MSA_Operator_Stewardship_20261008.docx). Key points summarized inline below so Raj's team can triage:

1) License scope (proposed):
- "Redwood grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, runtime-only license to use the Model(s) within Customer's designated private environment for Customer's internal business purposes. Customer shall not distribute, sublicense, or otherwise make model weights available outside the designated private environment except as expressly set forth in this exhibit."

2) Operator access:
- Access granted to named operator identities with just-in-time, auditable session tokens; operator activity is logged and subject to Customer review. We propose a max of 5 operator seats by default, adjustable by Order Form.

3) Snapshot / stewardship pathway:
- In limited continuity events (defined: vendor insolvency, prolonged unavailability > 30 days, or regulatory order), Redwood will provide a verified, read-only snapshot. Options: (a) encrypted artifact delivered to Customer KMS; (b) transfer to mutually agreed third-party steward for verification. We added a requirement for mutually-signed transfer acceptance to avoid tampering disputes.

4) Evidence & audit artifacts:
- We can commit to sharing SOC2 summary, runbook excerpts, and a sample snapshot checklist. Full SOC2 reports require an NDA/secured exchange (link in attachment).

5) KMS / keys:
- Customer-managed KMS is acceptable; operator keys for emergency access will be wrapped by customer KMS with a time-limited unwrap window. We added a heartbeat / automated revoke clause.

Open items for CyteHealth to confirm: whether the customer wants a full artifact transfer (weights/tokenizer) or the stewarded snapshot option; and the retention window for logs (we proposed 90 days).

I recommend we run this by Procurement & Security and produce the clean redline + an Order Form exhibit that enumerates seat counts and transfer triggers.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redline_MSA_Operator_Stewardship_20261008.docx]
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cytechealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@cytechealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline: Operator Stewardship exhibit + license carveouts

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from CyteHealth Legal/Security:

- We prefer the stewarded snapshot option (b) over a direct transfer of weights to our environment due to regulatory constraints. Having a mutually agreed third-party steward who can attest to the snapshot is preferable.
- For logs, our minimum request is 12 months for auditability, though we understand you may have retention/cost tradeoffs — can you confirm what is feasible?
- For KMS: yes, we want the option for customer-managed KMS. For the emergency unwrap window, can the timeout be 24 hours with an audit trail delivered to our security team?

If you can update the redline to (a) mark the steward path as the primary deliverable and (b) propose a logs retention cost schedule (90 days default + optional paid 12 month), we can push this through procurement.

Best,
Raj
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cytechealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline: Operator Stewardship exhibit + license carveouts

Perfect — next steps and delivery plan:

1) Rishi will produce a marked redline that: (i) elevates the stewarded-snapshot pathway as preferred, (ii) inserts a logs retention appendix with pricing tiers (90d included; 12mo as paid add-on), and (iii) sets the emergency unwrap window to 24 hours with full audit exports. Target: EOD Oct 9 (Rishi) — otherwise Monday morning.

2) Lauren will package a 2-page runbook excerpt and the sample snapshot checklist for your Security review by Oct 9 COB.

3) Stephanie (me) will produce a short procurement checklist (PO terms, order form exhibit layout, seat counts) and a proposed Order Form template that binds the exhibit to the Order Form. I will send that in a separate email to Raj + Procurement contacts.

If CyteHealth can confirm the steward vendor preference (we have pre-vetted stewards we can propose), we can include the steward name in the redline.

Thanks everyone — looks like we're aligned to get this into your procurement window.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
